Unlike traditional ML, active learning involves iterative cycles of prediction and experimentation, using a surrogate model trained on labeled data alongside an acquisition function to select high-uncertainty, unlabeled data points for further testing.
Ultimately, active learning provides a time- and resource-efficient method for identifying data with superior target properties through focused experimentation.

The framework of active learning with multiple objectives, the Pareto active learning framework, is established with a Gaussian process regressor (GPR), initially trained with 119 different combinations of LPBF process parameters and HT conditions from previous studies, employed as the surrogate model, and expected hypervolume improvement (EHVl) used as the acquisition function.
